newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi says will back Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi says will back Albania force.

text.p: Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Wednesday that he expected his centre-right alliance to vote in favour of the deployment of Italian troops in Albania at the head of a planned multinational security force.

The former prime minister, who crossed swords with the government at the weekend over its policy on Albania, said the proposed force was needed to help restore order ahead of planned early elections in the Balkan state.
"I don't think Italy can exclude itself from being present, at the head of other forces, in restoring order in Albania," the Freedom Alliance opposition bloc leader told reporters.
"It is the only means we see of resolving the problem of mass emigration to our country," he added.

Italy has offered to lead a multinational force of some 5,000 men that is being prepared to accompany a European humanitarian relief mission to troubled areas. The deployment will require approval by both houses of parliament.
Backing from the Berlusconi bloc would ensure wide support for the deployment despite divisions in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition.
The Greens and the hard left party Communist Refoundation, both government supporters, say they oppose the force.
Berlusconi criticised government policy on Albania at the weekend when he visited survivors from an Albanian refugee boat that sank after it was in collision with an Italian navy corvette.

The media mogul called on the government to end naval interdiction patrols which Italy introduced in the Adriatic after some 13,000 Albanians fled to southeastern ports in an uncontrolled exodus from the chaos in their homeland.
